title: Polynomial-Time Branching by Comparison
statement: Let $f,g$ map Boolean words to natural numbers, and let $a,b$ map Boolean words to Boolean words. If the unary encodings of $f$ and $g$, and the word functions $a$ and $b$, are polynomial-time computable, then the function that returns $a(z)$ when $f(z)<g(z)$ and $b(z)$ otherwise is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: The unary word function $z\mapsto 1^{f(z)}$ is polynomial-time computable
The unary word function $z\mapsto 1^{g(z)}$ is polynomial-time computable
The word function $a$ is polynomial-time computable
The word function $b$ is polynomial-time computable
replaced: If two unary values and two word functions are polynomial-time computable, then so is the function returning the first word when the first value is strictly smaller and the second word otherwise.
